summary: Build OT risk, IEC 62443, and incident-response skills in 5 days. Train your team to secure industrial systems with practical exercises.
lede: Operational technology training equips professionals across operations, engineering, maintenance, security, and risk to reduce cyber exposure while preserving safety and uptime. Participants practice inventorying industrial assets, mapping Purdue levels and security zones, assessing risk, reviewing remote access, and planning incident response and recovery for control-system environments.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who work on or around industrial operations and need to reduce cyber risk without weakening safety or uptime. It suits you if your role sits between operations, engineering, maintenance, security, or risk governance and you need practical OT security outputs.
prerequisites: Participants should have working knowledge of industrial operations, control system environments, or cybersecurity fundamentals. A general understanding of OT components such as SCADA, PLCs, HMI systems, industrial networks, and remote access workflows is recommended. No programming is required, but you should be comfortable reviewing network diagrams, risk registers, and policy or incident-response templates. A laptop and access to standard office software are required for workshop exercises. Advanced technical concepts such as IEC 62443 zone design and incident-response coordination will be taught at an operational application level rather than as production engineering or deep protocol reverse-engineering.
